newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes ease Wednesday, talk of deal - Sept 4.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes ease Wednesday, talk of deal - Sept 4.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices eased Wednesday, following a crude futures market which fell on news Iraq withdrew forces from Kurdish safe havens in northern Iraq.
West Texas Intermediate cash prices, the basis for West Coast light grades, also fell to $23.15/23.25 a barrel, off 15 cents from late Tuesday levels.
Most traders said Alaska North Slope crude discounts off WTI remained flat at minus $2.05, though one claimed a deal was done today at $2.20 under.
The wider differential reflected a market well supplied by leftovers from refinery problems in California.
Chevron, Mobil and Arco were rumored to experience problems, traders said, with Mobil's Los Angeles-area fluid catalytic cracker forecast to return later this week.
Traders said refineries that normally buy were seen selling Alaska North Slope crude today because they had bought foreign cargoes.
One Northwest refinery offered crude at $2.10 off October WTI, while an L.A. refinery sold October ANS at prices based on the monthly average of September.

And a major producer of ANS bought Koch Alberta Canadian crudes to ease competition and also help Canadian producers remove the excess grade from West Coast markets. The producer is rumored to offer the crude overseas.
Discounts for heavy and light grades could widen on a postings basis because Chevron Corp raised its postings 50 cents late Tuesday, traders said.
The rise in postings tracked yesterday's NYMEX rally.
Values for Kern River stayed unchanged after rising with postings Tuesday.
Line 63 differentials were unchanged at WTI minus $2.60/2.50 a barrel, with little trading seen ahead of mid-September.
